articles.title: I played static to Whisper. It said it was going to the next room.
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Spirit Box turns off every filter that keeps OpenAI's open Whisper quiet, then plays it pure noise. It…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Spirit Box turns off every filter that keeps OpenAI's open Whisper quiet, then plays it pure noise. It talks. Silence gets "you", every time. Mains hum gets "I'm going to go to the next room." , eleven times a clip. It never leaves. Those ghosts also turn up in real transcripts with normal settings ( Koenecke et al., 2024 found them in about 1% of clips), where they look like every other line. So the second half is a witness : Gemma 3 4B, running locally, reads a meeting transcript and points at the lines nobody said. Demo Live: https://spirit-box-hacktoberfest.vercel.app . Pick a noise, press Summon, and Whisper tiny listens in your browser tab. No audio leaves it.

The modern imitation learning playbook—Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), Diffusion Policies, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models—has made impressive strides on 6-DoF parallel jaw grippers. But moving from a rigid two-finger clamp to a 16-to-24 DoF dexterous multi-finger hand reveals a fundamental physics barrier: vision cannot observe contact state once the hand touches the object. articles.body: Werbung / Disclosure: Prisma gave me a coupon for two months of a paid plan for free and said it will add free credits, so I could try Prisma Postgres and Compute for this project. All results below come from my own runs. Summary I built an order flow with a 10-minute grace period. Cancel and send must have exactly one winner. The winner is decided in Postgres, with a guarded update, a row lock and SKIP LOCKED . No clock and no timer decides it. I broke the code on purpose, one line at a time, to check that my tests really fail. One of my race tests passed even without the lock. On Compute, an idle app sleeps. articles.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
articles.excerpt: Confined inside a research station 22 feet (7 meters) underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew performed research and maintenance activities like future astronauts on Mars.
articles.body: Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place.

articles.title: ISS astronaut will conduct Canada's 1st spacewalk in 7 years on Oct. 29: Watch it live
articles.excerpt: Joshua Kutryk will venture outside the International Space Station on Oct. 29, on the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut in more than seven years. Here's how to watch it live.
articles.body: The next International Space Station (ISS) spacewalk will have more maple-leaf flavor than usual, as a Canadian astronaut will become the first to go outside the orbiting complex in seven years. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who's also a colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force, will help the ISS boost its power supply during his first-ever spacewalk on Thursday (Oct. 29). Kutryk will be joined by NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who has done three spacewalks already and also serves as a colonel with the U.S. Space Force . The duo are scheduled to venture outside the orbiting lab at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), kicking off a spacewalk that will last roughly 6 hours and 45 minutes. You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 6:30 a.m. EDT (1030 GMT).

(Image credit: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor) A U.S. military intelligence agency has released an incredible new photograph of China's secretive space plane, showing it docked to another spacecraft in orbit. The photograph was taken in 2024 by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite, from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers).
